# Poe2SkillBarAccessor

[API index](../index.md)

Current player hotbar, including empty slots and their actual game bindings.
Supports mouse/keyboard and WASD; controller or unreadable data returns null from lookups.
Read again for updated skills/readiness; game bindings normally refresh every 100 ms.
Slots are logical skill buttons, not UI Elements or screen coordinates. See recipe 11-skill-hotkeys.ts.

**@keywords**

skills, hotbar, bindings, keyboard, slots

## Slots

```typescript
Slots: Poe2SkillBarSlot[] | null;
```

All 13 slots; null when the server bar or active input bindings are unavailable.
Empty slots retain their hotkey and have Skill.Exists=false.
A skill assigned to multiple slots appears once per slot; never filter empty slots before indexing.

**@keywords**

skills, hotbar, enumerate, empty, availability

## BySlotIndex

```typescript
BySlotIndex(index: number): Poe2SkillBarSlot | null;
```

A zero-based slot, or null for an invalid index or unavailable bar/bindings.
Slot indices are positions, not keyboard keys; use ByHotkey to resolve a key.

**@keywords**

skills, hotbar, slot, index, binding

## ByHotkey

```typescript
ByHotkey(hotkey: Key | string): Poe2SkillBarSlot | null;
```

Resolve one slot by its actual key or chord, such as Key.W or "Ctrl+W".
Returns null when unavailable or unmatched; throws for invalid syntax or multiple matching slots.
"MouseRight" and "Ctrl+MouseRight" resolve mouse buttons; modifiers are part of the exact match.

**Example**

```ts
const slot = World.SkillBar.ByHotkey(Key.W);
Log(slot === null ? "No readable W slot" : `${slot.Hotkey}: ${slot.Skill.Name}`);
```

**See also**

World.SkillBar.AllByHotkey

**@keywords**

skills, hotbar, hotkey, binding, reverse lookup

## AllByHotkey

```typescript
AllByHotkey(hotkey: Key | string): Poe2SkillBarSlot[] | null;
```

All slots assigned to the exact key/chord; empty when unmatched, null when unavailable.
Invalid hotkey syntax throws. Duplicate skill identities remain separate slots.
An empty matched slot has Skill.Exists=false; it is different from an empty result array.

**Example**

```ts
const slots = World.SkillBar.AllByHotkey("Ctrl+W");
Log(JSON.stringify(slots?.map(slot => ({ index: slot.Index, name: slot.Skill.Name })) ?? null));
```

**@keywords**

skills, hotbar, hotkey, duplicates, enumerate
